panels.title: Backends the router lists
panels.description: How many deployments litellm_deployment_state currently reports, which is the router's own table rather than anything scraped off a serving box. Red is not a threshold here: fewer rows than litellm/config.yaml declares means the proxy loaded a shorter model list than you think, and the missing model has no backend at all.

panels.title: Backends off the healthy state
panels.description: litellm:deployments_not_ready, the count of deployments whose litellm_deployment_state is off 0, as the router's background health checks last saw it. Any value above 0 is red: the router has stopped sending that deployment traffic, and with one deployment per model group that model has no working backend.

panels.title: Cooldown transitions, last 15m
panels.description: Summed litellm:cooldown_events:15m, the number of times the router pulled any deployment out of rotation in the last 15 minutes. This is the whole cooldown surface at this LiteLLM tag: there is no remaining-cooldown gauge, so a box that recovers and fails again shows up as a growing count here rather than as a timer.

panels.title: Admission backlog (proxy-wide)
panels.description: litellm_admission_queued_requests summed over the proxy: requests held by admission rather than being served. It carries no labels and is counted per uvicorn worker, so a proxy-wide sum is the finest honest read and no backend can be named from it. A sustained backlog means the queue, not a serving box, is setting the latency callers see.

panels.title: Deployment inventory and state
panels.description: One row per deployment the router knows about, keyed model_id and api_base, which is the only place on this page that prints the upstream base URL. The state column is litellm_deployment_state: 0 healthy, 1 partial outage, 2 complete outage. A box that is switched off is legitimately 2; a box parked at 1 is the one to open a shell on.

panels.title: Liveness the stack sees (scrape and probe)
panels.description: Not LiteLLM's own view: up for the litellm scrape target answers whether the proxy is publishing metrics at all, and probe_success and probe_http_status_code for the blackbox-spark-models job answer whether the model endpoints behind it answer HTTP. These series carry the scrape target, not model_id, so the two filters above do not reach them and a 0 names an endpoint that is not answering, not a particular deployment.

panels.title: Request rate per deployment
panels.description: litellm_deployment_total_requests_total per deployment: what the router actually dispatched, which is the number the least-busy picker is working from. A flat line here while the model keeps answering is the serving box having stopped taking work; two aliases landing on the same backend shows as two lines that always move together.

panels.title: Error ratio per deployment
panels.description: That deployment's own failure responses over its own dispatched requests, both from litellm_deployment_failure_responses_total and litellm_deployment_total_requests_total and both keyed model_id, so the join is exact and a lightly loaded box is not punished by a shared denominator. Red means the router is losing the traffic it sent to this backend; a backend with no traffic in the window simply has no line rather than a clean 0.

panels.title: Failures per deployment by upstream status
panels.description: litellm_deployment_failure_responses_total split by the upstream status the serving box returned, so a 500 from one backend is not blended into a 400 from another. Read it beside the fallback panel below: a failure here with nothing behind it there was raised inside the proxy rather than returned by a box.

panels.title: Cooldown transitions per deployment
panels.description: increase() of litellm_deployment_cooled_down_total over 15 minutes per model_id and api_base: how often the router pulled this one deployment out of rotation. This is the flap detector, since a box with a short cooldown_time can be cooled constantly and still look healthy under traffic, and there is no cooldown-duration gauge at this tag to contradict it.

panels.title: Fallbacks raised, by model group
panels.description: litellm_deployment_successful_fallbacks_total and litellm_deployment_failed_fallbacks_total over 5m, split by requested_model, fallback_model and exception_class. Those counters are keyed on the model group and not on model_id, so this panel says which group lost its primary and not which deployment took the hand-off, and there is no router retry counter at this tag, so this is net fallback volume only.

panels.title: Request latency p50/p95/p99 per deployment
panels.description: The recorded total-latency quantiles per model_id, which is what a caller routed to that backend waits for. p95 climbing while p50 sits still means one class of request on this backend is hurting; all three moving together means the box itself slowed down.

panels.title: Upstream p95 against total p95, per deployment
panels.description: The recorded upstream quantile (litellm_llm_api_latency_metric_bucket, the part the serving box owns) plotted against the total quantile for the same model_id. The gap is the proxy's work on that request: a wide gap is this stack's problem, lines locked together mean the box is genuinely slow.

panels.title: Proxy overhead share (proxy-wide)
panels.description: litellm:overhead_share:5m, the overhead histogram as a share of total latency. It is charted proxy-wide on purpose: the overhead histogram carries no backend label on the surface these rules are pinned to, so the repo's own recording rule aggregates it across the proxy and no per-backend split is honest here. Rising while the upstream quantiles stay flat is the proxy costing the caller time.

panels.title: Tokens per second per backend
panels.description: The recorded prompt, completion and total token rates per model_id, which is the per-backend key the token counters actually carry: they publish no api_base, so a backend is named here by its model_id and never by a URL. A completion line that collapses while the prompt line holds is a box still accepting work and failing to finish it.

panels.title: Tokens generated per request, per backend
panels.description: The recorded completion-token rate over the recorded per-backend request rate, both keyed model_id, so the division is exact and the reading is how much each backend is generating per request it takes. There is no tokens-in-flight series at this tag, so this is the closest per-backend answer to work in progress; the two rules are recorded over 1m and 5m, so treat it as a level rather than an instantaneous count.

panels.title: Latency per output token (proxy-wide)
panels.description: litellm:latency_per_output_token_p95:5m, seconds per generated token from litellm_deployment_latency_per_output_token_bucket: how fast the serving boxes decode. Proxy-wide because the recorded rule keys this histogram on le alone, so there is no honest per-backend split on the surface this repo pins to; read it against the per-backend completion rate in this row, since a backend that is slow shows up there first. Rising means generation itself got slower, not the queue.

panels.title: Queue wait (proxy-wide)
panels.description: litellm:queue_wait_p50:5m and p95, the time a request waits between admission and dispatch. Proxy-wide because this repo's own rules aggregate the queue histogram by le alone, so the series carries no backend label and cannot name which deployment a request was waiting on. A p95 past 0.5s means every deployment stayed busy while callers queued.

panels.title: Admission rejections by reason
panels.description: litellm:admission_rejections_per_second:5m, the requests admission refused outright rather than queued, split by reason. Any line above zero is red: the reason is the finding, because a budget reason means the rpm and token limits are the binding constraint and anything else is admission refusing work it should have queued. Proxy-wide, for the same label-less reason as the backlog stat at the top.

panels.title: Admission budget headroom (proxy-wide)
panels.description: The tightest remaining request and token budget the proxy reports, from litellm_remaining_requests_metric and litellm_remaining_tokens_metric. Charted as the minimum rather than per backend because neither gauge is keyed on model_id by any rule in this repo, so naming a backend from them would be an invented join. Heading for 0 is the panel that explains a rejection spike beside it.

panels.title: Balance per deployment
panels.description: One row per backend with the five numbers that decide whether the fleet is even: dispatched rate, p95 total latency, completion tokens per second, router state, and cooldown transitions over the last hour. Each column is its own query keyed model_id, so a cell that is empty is a backend with no traffic in the window rather than a zero. Read the rate column across before the latency column.

panels.title: Deployment rate spread per model group
panels.description: The busiest deployment's dispatched rate over the quietest one in the same requested_model group, from litellm_deployment_total_requests_total, which carries model_id and requested_model together so the grouping is real and not a join. A line sitting near 1 is an even group; a line climbing into the tens is one deployment taking the group while another is starved or quietly out of rotation.

targets.expr: max by (requested_model) (sum by (model_id, requested_model) (rate(litellm_deployment_total_requests_total{model_id=~"$deployment", requested_model=~"$requested_model"}[5m]))) / (min by (requested_model) (sum by (model_id, requested_model) (rate(litellm_deployment_total_requests_total{model_id=~"$deployment", requested_model=~"$requested_model"}[5m]))) > 0)

panels.title: Aliases served per deployment
panels.description: How many requested_model values each model_id appears under in the router's dispatch counter over the selected range: the model inventory as the backends actually experienced it, one row per backend. A deployment that should serve three aliases and shows one has been left out of a model group, which no other panel on this page says.

panels.title: Model-list endpoints the probe covers
panels.description: How many targets the blackbox-spark-models job is probing right now, which is the model-list inventory the stack expects rather than what any serving box reports about itself. It is counted proxy-wide because the probe series carry a scrape target and no model_id, so they cannot be attributed to a backend; a drop here means the stack lost sight of endpoints, which is a monitoring gap before it is an inference fault.
